name: Atlantic coasts and northern / western inland lakes — format: tools/spots/README.md
Bray-Dunes
notes: Huge flat beach next to the Belgian border; shallow at low tide, more chop at high tide.

name: Malo-les-Bains (Dunkerque)
notes: Dunkerque Flysurfing Club beach; very wide at low tide.

name: Gravelines – Petit-Fort-Philippe
notes: 'Petite mer' behind the sandbank: flat water around high tide with big coefficients, open sea outside. Buoyed kite zone.

name: Les Hemmes de Marck
notes: Very wide gently sloping beach, flattish water behind sandbanks; best in NW to NE winds.

name: Calais – Blériot-Plage
notes: Watch the wooden groynes at high tide.

name: Sangatte
notes: Windiest spot of the Côte d'Opale, long waves; groynes on the beach. Kite school on site.

name: Wissant
notes: Between the two capes (venturi): powerful wind and waves, experienced riders.

name: Wimereux – Pointe aux Oies
notes: Waves; Wimereux town beach only works at low tide, the Pointe aux Oies is the main launch.

name: Le Portel
notes: Kite school on the beach; waves in westerlies.

name: Hardelot
notes: Flat water in the low-tide pools (baïnes) and waves outside.

name: Le Touquet
notes: Launch north of Aqualud; the Canche bay works in E winds around high tide (strong currents).

name: Berck-sur-Mer
notes: Huge beach; flat pools at low tide.

name: Fort-Mahon-Plage
notes: Kite school zone north of the nautical base.

name: Le Crotoy
notes: Tidal bay: rideable around high tide only. Do not cross the yellow buoys of the nature reserve.

name: Cayeux-sur-Mer – La Mollière
notes: Between Cayeux and Le Hourdel; kite schools and club in Cayeux.

name: Quiberville
notes: Marked kite zone (mandatory); works WSW to NW. Pebble beach, sand at low tide.

name: Le Havre
notes: Urban pebble beach, kite schools; works in SW to NW winds.

name: Merville-Franceville
notes: Dedicated kite zone at the west end of Boulevard Wattier, open all year (the only kite beach in July–August). Keep out of the bird reserve at the Orne estuary to the west.

name: Ouistreham – Riva-Bella
notes: Low tide only: at high tide the water reaches the sea wall.

name: Asnelles
notes: Mulberry harbour remains offshore; summer: kiting usually only outside bathing hours.

name: Utah Beach
notes: Huge beach; best at low to mid tide.

name: Cherbourg – Collignon
notes: Flat water inside the Cherbourg breakwater, around high tide; works W to NE.

name: Siouville-Hague
notes: Wave spot, all tides.

name: Jullouville
notes: Best from mid to low tide.

name: Cherrueix
notes: Bay of Mont-Saint-Michel: huge tidal range; ride around high tide.

name: Saint-Malo – Le Sillon
notes: 1 Jul–1 Sep: mandatory launch zone between the Kyriad hotel and Avenue Fuentès. Beach disappears at high spring tides.

name: Saint-Lunaire – Longchamp
notes: Banned 10:00–20:00 from 15 June to 15 September.

name: Lancieux
notes: Flat, shallow bay; best at low tide. July–August: Saint-Sieu beach is closed, launch at Tête de Chien (low tide) or Roche Morin (high tide).

name: Sables-d'Or-les-Pins
notes: Wide shallow beach, mixed sand / shallow water.

name: Erquy – Caroual
notes: Kite zone away from the bathing area; best in SW to NW winds.

name: Hillion – Bon Abri
notes: Bay of Saint-Brieuc: huge tidal range, ride mid to high tide. Nature reserve nearby.

name: Plérin – Les Rosaires
notes: Easterly-wind spot; busy with families in summer, ride off-season.

name: Keremma
notes: 5 km of beach between the Kernic and Goulven bays; flat water at low tide.

name: Landéda – Sainte-Marguerite
notes: Sheltered; flat water at low tide. Summer kite zone.

name: Lampaul-Ploudalmézeau – Trois Moutons
notes: Tréompan dunes; calm water, beach narrows at high tide. Summer kite zone.

name: Le Conquet – Blancs Sablons
locate: q:Plage des Blancs Sablons Le Conquet

name: Brest – Moulin Blanc
notes: Flat water in the Rade de Brest, gusty wind. Closed 1 July–31 August 09:00–19:00.

name: Crozon – Goulien
notes: Waves; main kite beach of the Crozon peninsula.

name: La Torche
notes: Kiters launch north of the point (Tronoën), away from the surfers; waves.

name: Île-Tudy
notes: Flat shallow water at low tide and early flood; works E to SW. Summer: banned 12:00–19:00, keep out of the bathing zones.

name: Bénodet – Lagune du Letty
notes: Flat-water lagoon (Mer Blanche) behind the dune spit, launch at the slipway below the UCPA. Around high tide, preferably on the flood (strong ebb currents); best in S to E winds.

name: Fort-Bloqué
notes: Waves; rocks mid-spot, best mid to low tide.

name: Gâvres
notes: Ocean beach (waves) or the flat Petite Mer de Gâvres from mid tide.

name: Erdeven – Kerhillio
notes: Ride from 3 h before to 3 h after low tide. 15 June–15 September: kite zone in the east sector (beach accesses 27–28); banned around high tide at big coefficients (> 85).

name: Penthièvre
notes: Bay side of the Penthièvre isthmus (flat water, oyster shells) and ocean side. Only 3 h either side of low tide. Late May–mid September: bay side banned, ocean-side kite zones at accesses 1 and 10–11.

name: Plouharnel – Les Sables Blancs
notes: Bay side of the Quiberon isthmus for NE to SE winds; best at low to mid tide, choppy higher up. Avoid the oyster parks (poles, yellow buoys ~500 m out); wear booties.

name: Sarzeau – Penvins
notes: Shallow basin, flat around high tide; beginner-friendly.

name: Assérac – Pont-Mahé
notes: Shallow bay, you can stand almost everywhere; kite schools.

name: La Turballe – Pen Bron
notes: Wave spot, shore break; little beach at high tide (sea wall).

name: La Baule
notes: Plage Benoît: flat water behind the sandbank at low tide, kite schools. 15 June–15 September: banned from the beach, experienced riders only via the K13 channel at the La Baule / Pornichet border.

name: Saint-Brevin-les-Pins
notes: 15 June–15 September (and weekends from May): kiting only in the signposted zone, schools at the Plage du Billard.

name: Fromentine
notes: Flat water in the channel facing Noirmoutier, best 2 h either side of low tide. Summer: kite zone right of the bathing area; keep out of the ferry channel.

name: Notre-Dame-de-Monts
notes: Wide beach at low tide.

name: Bretignolles-sur-Mer
notes: Kite zone on the Plage des Dunes, buoyed in July–August.

name: La Tranche-sur-Mer
notes: Plage du Phare, facing Île de Ré: waves and current, good level needed. May–September: the only beach where kiting is allowed.

name: Île de Ré – Rivedoux
notes: North beach, marked kite zone; flat, works NW to NE. Oyster beds reduce space at low tide.

name: Île de Ré – Les Portes (Trousse-Chemise)
notes: Flat shallow bay with a sandbank at low tide; works N to E. Strong currents near the Fier d'Ars.

name: La Rochelle – Aytré
notes: Muddy shallow bay, ride 2 h either side of high tide; works SW to NW.

name: Châtelaillon-Plage
notes: Kite area south of the main beach; all tides.

name: Oléron – Plage des Huttes
notes: Flat basin behind the reef around low tide, shore break at high tide. Avoid the bathing zones in summer.

name: Oléron – Plaisance
notes: Works N to E, all tides; marked kite zone in summer.

name: Oléron – La Perroche
notes: Rocks, intermediate riders; banned in summer.

name: Oléron – Gatseau
notes: Shallow south-facing bay; flat around high tide.

name: La Palmyre – Bonne Anse
notes: Sheltered shallow bay, best on the rising tide (strong ebb currents).

name: Le Verdon – La Chambrette
notes: Estuary beach for E to NE winds, 2 h either side of high tide.

name: Lac d'Hourtin-Carcans
notes: Lake: flat water; stay south of the yellow buoy line.

name: Lacanau-Océan
notes: Waves, experienced riders. Summer: kiting before 19:00 only in the Super-Sud zone.

name: Lac de Lacanau
notes: Lake: flat water; use the marked channel in summer.

name: Bassin d'Arcachon – Claouey
notes: Tidal basin, 2–3 h either side of high tide; muddy bottom, oyster shells. Closed July–August.

name: Bassin d'Arcachon – Andernos (Le Bétey)
notes: Tidal basin, around high tide only. Closed July–August.

name: Bassin d'Arcachon – Les Arbousiers
notes: Sandbank at low tide, strong current at high tide. Banned in summer.

name: Bassin d'Arcachon – La Hume
notes: Tidal basin: ride around high tide. Closed in the hunting season (October–November).

name: La Teste – La Salie
notes: Ocean beach at the south end of the basin entrance; supervised zone late June–early September.

name: Lac de Cazaux – Navarrosse
notes: Flat, shallow lake (Cazaux-Sanguinet), south shore. Navarrosse launch September–May; June–August use the kite zone at Mayotte (just east).

name: Lac de Sanguinet – Port de l'Estey
notes: Water launch, intermediate riders; avoid the buoyed zone to the north.

name: Biscarrosse-Plage
notes: Waves; summer kite zone south of the bathing area.

name: Mimizan
notes: Plage Sud kite zone; keep away from the river mouth currents.

name: Contis
notes: Watch the jetties near the river mouth.

name: Moliets
notes: Waves; large area near the Huchet river mouth, best at high tide.

name: Seignosse – Les Estagnots
notes: Waves and current, experienced riders. Only Seignosse beach where kiting is allowed; June–September: signposted zone south of the car park during bathing hours.

name: Anglet – La Madrague
notes: Waves, experienced riders. Allowed November–May; in season only early morning and after 19:00 via the marked channel.

name: Hendaye
notes: Only Basque beach without cliffs. Banned 1 July–31 August.

name: Lac du Der – Giffaumont
notes: Kite zone regulated by the local club (KDA); red zone closed 15 June–15 September.

name: Lac d'Orient – Mesnil-Saint-Père
notes: Experienced riders, March to October, through the local clubs (AWA, Flysurf10); beaches closed 15 June–15 September.

name: Lac de Madine
notes: Club-only (AKL membership and FFVL licence required); main beach for SW–W winds, gusty.
